errors.name: Jesse Owens
errors.reason: Owens' competitive track career ended in 1936; he was barred from amateur competition by the AAU shortly after the Berlin Olympics. In the 1940s he only did exhibition/promotional races, not competitive athletics. (Statement: Gordie Howe / Jackie Robinson / Jesse Owens / Ted Williams)

errors.name: Robert Parish
errors.reason: Parish famously wore No. 00 (double zero), not No. 0 — a distinct jersey number. Lillard, Tatum, and Westbrook all wore 0. (Statement: Damian Lillard / Jayson Tatum / Robert Parish / Russell Westbrook)

naming_notes: Tennessee Titans lanes: Earl Campbell and Warren Moon played for the franchise only in its Houston Oilers era (pre-1999 rename); Campbell appears in two Titans statements and Moon in three.
Las Vegas Raiders lane (Dickerson/Rice/Lynch/Moss): all four played only in the Los Angeles/Oakland Raiders eras, never in Las Vegas.
Washington Nationals lanes: Pedro Martinez (1994-97), Pete Rose (1984), and Randy Johnson (1988-89) played for the franchise only as the Montreal Expos, never in Washington.
Oklahoma City Thunder lanes (3 statements): Patrick Ewing played for the franchise only as the Seattle SuperSonics (2000-01), never in Oklahoma City.
Atlanta Braves lanes (3 statements): Babe Ruth played for the franchise only as the Boston Braves (1935), never in Atlanta.
Indianapolis Colts lane: Johnny Unitas played for the franchise only as the Baltimore Colts.
Golden State Warriors lane: Wilt Chamberlain played for the franchise as the Philadelphia/San Francisco Warriors, before the Golden State rename.
Washington Commanders lanes: Bruce Smith, Deion Sanders, and Adrian Peterson played for the franchise under the Redskins name (same city, renamed 2020/2022).
St. Louis Cardinals lane: Cy Young played for the franchise in 1899-1900 (Perfectos era; the Cardinals name was just being adopted in 1900).
